html:
The Osage Nation is the reservation and government of the Osage people in northeastern Oklahoma, covering what is now Osage County. The Osage, a Dhegiha Siouan people, had once dominated much of the Missouri and Arkansas river country as hunters and traders, allied in turn with the French and the Spanish; the map shows that earlier homeland as Osage.

US treaties in 1808 and 1825 took most of their land and moved them to a reserve in Kansas. In the early 1870s they sold it and bought this tract in Indian Territory from the Cherokee. Oil was found beneath it, and because the Osage kept the mineral rights in common, each member's share, or headright, brought large royalties. In the 1920s outsiders murdered dozens of Osage to get those headrights, the Osage Indian murders investigated by the young Bureau of Investigation, later the FBI. Their relatives the Kaw and Ponca live on neighbouring lands.
